hints: Start by matching each ventricle to where it sends blood. Which one pumps into the aorta for the whole body, and which one pumps into the pulmonary artery for the nearby lungs?
Remember the link given in the stem: more shortening fibres means more force, which means more pressure. Which side needs much higher pressure to overcome greater resistance?
walkthrough:
**Recall the two different journeys**

Think of the heart as two pumps side by side. The right ventricle pumps blood a short distance to the lungs via the pulmonary artery. The left ventricle pumps blood all around the body via the aorta.

That body route is much longer and has much higher resistance, so it needs much higher pressure.

**Link muscle thickness to pressure**

The stem tells us that shortening muscle fibres create force, and force creates pressure on blood. So a thicker wall with more muscle fibres can contract with more force and generate more pressure.

**Pick the correct explanation**

The left ventricle wall is much thicker than the right ventricle wall. Its greater number of fibres gives a stronger contraction and higher pressure to push blood into the aorta and around the body. That matches option B perfectly.

options.A: This reverses the facts. The left ventricle is thicker, and more pressure is needed to push blood into the aorta than into the pulmonary artery.
options.B: Correct. The left ventricle has more muscle fibres, so contraction produces more force and higher pressure needed for systemic circulation.
options.C: The difference in thickness is not about chamber volume. Both ventricles pump similar volumes, the difference is the pressure needed for the different distances.
options.D: This reverses the facts. The left ventricle wall is thicker, and it is the left side that generates and withstands the higher pressure.
